history.heading: Great Zimbabwe
paragraphs: Zimbabwe takes its name from Great Zimbabwe, a stone city built by ancestors of the Shona people between the 11th and 15th centuries. It was the capital of a wealthy kingdom that traded gold and ivory with the Swahili coast and beyond, and its ruins are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Mutapa and Rozvi states followed. In the 19th century, the Ndebele kingdom was established in the southwest.

history.heading: Rhodesia
paragraphs: Cecil Rhodes's British South Africa Company colonised the territory in the 1890s, naming it Rhodesia and crushing Ndebele and Shona uprisings (the First Chimurenga). White settlers took the best land. Southern Rhodesia became a self-governing British colony in 1923.

In 1965 the white minority government of Ian Smith declared independence unilaterally to avoid majority rule. A liberation war (the Second Chimurenga) followed, led by ZANU and ZAPU, killing tens of thousands, until the 1979 Lancaster House Agreement.

history.heading: Independent Zimbabwe
paragraphs: Zimbabwe became independent on 18 April 1980, with Robert Mugabe as leader. In the 1980s the Gukurahundi massacres in Matabeleland killed thousands. From 2000 a fast-track land reform programme seized most white-owned farms, which, along with mismanagement, caused economic collapse and hyperinflation in 2007–2008.
In 2017 a military intervention forced Mugabe to resign after 37 years in power, and Emmerson Mnangagwa became president.

culture.heading: Traditions
paragraphs: Zimbabwe has 16 official languages, of which Shona, Ndebele and English are the most widely used. Most people are Christian, often combined with traditional beliefs in ancestral spirits. Zimbabwe has one of the highest literacy rates in Africa.

Shona stone sculpture is internationally renowned, and the mbira (thumb piano) is central to traditional music, recognised by UNESCO. Sadza, a thick maize porridge, is the staple food. Writers include Tsitsi Dangarembga.

politics.heading: Dominant party
paragraphs: Zimbabwe is a presidential republic dominated by ZANU-PF since independence. Elections, including in 2023, have been criticised by observers, and the opposition faces repression. Proposals to extend Mnangagwa's term beyond 2028 have been controversial.

economy.heading: Resources and instability
paragraphs: Zimbabwe has rich resources, including platinum, gold, diamonds, lithium (it is Africa's largest producer) and fertile land. Tobacco is a major export. Remittances from Zimbabweans abroad are important. Since hyperinflation, the country has used US dollars widely; it introduced a new gold-backed currency, the ZiG, in 2024. Poverty, unemployment and debt remain serious challenges.
